title: Capacity Intake Preflight: SLA Scorecard & GPU Classifier for Dedicated Enterprise Requests
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Create a compact, repeatable preflight and scorecard to qualify enterprise Dedicated capacity requests. The artifact will be used by Solutions, Sales, and PMs to: 1) produce an initial SLA commitment range (latency P50/P95, availability target, and throughput guarantees), 2) recommend a reserved throughput profile and GPU class, and 3) suggest scaling/fallback policies (bursting, cross-region failover, model fallbacks). This ticket builds a templated questionnaire, a numeric scoring rubric, and a guidance matrix mapping workload signals to recommended capacity profiles.
comments: 2025-02-12 - Kickoff: met with Solutions (R. Chen) and Sales eng (M. Alvarez). Agreed preflight needs to be <=10 mins to complete and produce a ranked recommendation (High/Medium/Low capacity).
2025-02-18 - Draft rubric uploaded to Confluence: /confluence/redwood/dedicated-intake-preflight. Feedback: include a separate security tag for customer-managed keys and compliance constraints.

2025-02-24 - Engineering (S. Patel) provided GPU family throughput baselines for common models (Llama2-13B, Llama2-70B, mix of quantized variants). Added latency impact multipliers for KV cache hit rates.
2025-03-01 - Design (N. Ruiz) mocked a single-page intake UI that surfaces an SLO heatmap and a recommended 'starter pack' (GPU class + reserved tokens/s) with an exportable summary for contracts.
2025-03-04 - Internal review with Legal flagged: SLA commit text must include explicit outage and force majeure clauses. Follow-up: add non-binding 'expected' ranges vs. contract SLA fields.
decisions: Use a 0-100 numeric score derived from five axes: peak TPS, sustained TPS, latency sensitivity, tail-latency penalty (P95 importance), and data isolation requirement.
Map score 80-100 => "high" reserved profile (dedicated GPU profile A: A100/8 or H100 equivalent), 50-79 => "medium" (mixed GPU pool + pinning), <50 => "low" (burst-first with soft guarantees).
Default SLA buckets: P50 target (50-150ms depending on model family), P95 target (2-4x P50), availability target of 99.9% for 'high' and 99.5% for 'medium' unless customer purchases premium SLA.

Scaling policy templates: preferred = autoscale within dedicated pool (fast scale policy, 60s cool-down), fallback = route to compatible quantized variant with graceful degradation, emergency = cross-region failover to reserved emergency capacity with lower throughput guarantees.
Include a mandatory field to capture 'expected token distribution' (short chat-like vs long-form generation) to choose KV cache strategy.
acceptance_criteria: A one-page questionnaire that can be completed in under 10 minutes and outputs a numeric score and recommended capacity profile.
Scoring rubric validated with two recent enterprise requests: Customer X (high throughput chat app) and Customer Y (low volume but long-sequence generation).
Engineer sign-off on GPU-class mapping and throughput baselines (SRE or Runtime team).
Legal and Finance review the suggested SLA wording and revenue implications for three example profiles.
Prototype UI mock in Figma linked from the intake page and an exportable summary PDF template for contract intake.
